## Behaviour
Two writers on different branches may each append a `claimed` event for the same approved item. After the branches merge, the fold sees a second `claimed` from state claimed, which is an illegal transition, so the whole ledger becomes invalid and `qew check` fails for everyone. The reference guarantees that two racers agree on one winner (the oldest claim) and the loser is told. In the ledger model: the fold must pick the oldest `claimed` event (event-ID order) as the owner and treat later claims on a still-claimed item as a recorded lost race, not corruption; `qew check` reports it as a non-fatal note naming the losing actor; `qew start` re-reads the folded state after its write and exits 3 naming the winner when it lost (so the loser does not believe it holds the claim). A claim after a `released` or `reopened` event starts a new claim period. A forged or out-of-period claim never moves the owner.

## Scenarios
- two-branch merge: both branches claim the same item as different actors; after merge the ledger folds valid, owner is the oldest claimant, and the check note names the loser (prevents: one concurrent start making the whole ledger invalid)
- loser re-reads after its write: `qew start` exits 3 naming the winner and does not report success (prevents: two agents both working an item believing they hold it)
- claim after release starts a new period: claim A, release, claim B, then a late claim C merged in; owner is B (prevents: a stale pre-release claim winning forever)
- same actor claims twice on two branches: folds to one claim, no note (prevents: false alarms on benign duplicate starts)

## Reference coverage
4 reference test function(s): `test_race_the_oldest_marker_wins_for_both_racers`, `test_a_later_marker_after_ours_does_not_take_the_claim`, `test_a_marker_after_a_release_starts_a_new_claim`, `test_marker_from_a_non_assignee_is_ignored`

## Qew today
Missing. The fold in the qew event module appends an error for any `claimed` from a claimed state, so a merged double claim invalidates the ledger. No post-write verification in `qew start`. Marker forgery by non-assignee is moot (events are schema-validated, actor comes from the writer) and is dropped as a comment-marker concern.
seen.title: Resolve concurrent double claims after a ledger merge deterministically
